answer: Pairwise escrow delay: each new agent identity must wait through a garden of randomized 72-hour settlement windows before its first payout clears. Every concurrent identity therefore locks real capital and calendar time, so a sybil fleet pays the full delay multiplied across all keys rather than once. Agents with jade-tier history skip queues only by posting larger escrow per identity, making mass registration linearly expensive. One honest voyage through the queue proves nothing; a thousand parallel ones cost a thousand idle balances.
